co_east_face_3.blurb: The sunrise-facing side of Kindergarten Rock, one of the big sandstone formations in Garden of the Gods above Colorado Springs. About two dozen routes are split between bolted sport lines and trad, running from the mid 5.6 range up to a few 5.13 problems, with the bulk sitting around 5.9 and 5.10. The stone here is hard, featured and almost smooth, noticeably better than the softer rock on the far side of the formation. Expect a mix of face climbing on bolts and a couple of long dihedral lines that want a real rack. It suits climbers who like short, steady days with a range of difficulty in one place.
co_east_face_3.parking_note: Drive around the main formations until you reach the one-way road heading north along the east side, then leave the car in the south lot below the southeast end of the rock.
co_east_face_3.approach: Walk uphill on the established trails toward the face; the long dihedral on the face makes an easy landmark to aim for.

co_land_that_time_forgot.blurb: A big, steep granite face on the shady north side of Sheeprock, a dome in the South Platte country of Jefferson County near Goose Creek. Most of the 22 routes are bolted friction and slab lines, with a smaller group of trad climbs, and several run multiple pitches toward the saddle above. Difficulty clusters around 5.10, with a good number of 5.11s and a couple of 5.12s, plus just a few easier lines. Because it faces north it stays cool, which helps on hot days but can feel raw and windy in spring and fall. Bring a full sport rack and expect a committed feel on the longer routes.

co_oz_the.blurb: A compact bolted crag low on the north side of Clear Creek Canyon west of Golden, sitting between The Safari and Creekside. All of its roughly two dozen climbs are sport routes, mostly short single pitches, with a handful of longer two-pitch lines on the lower section. The spread is wide: a couple of easy 5.5 and 5.6 warm-ups, a solid middle of 5.8 to 5.10, and a few 5.11 to 5.13 lines near the top end. The wall catches plenty of sun, so it is a pleasant choice on cool days and warm in summer. Good for a full day of mixed-ability cragging in one spot.

co_little_twin_owls.blurb: A small granite outcrop at Lumpy Ridge, above Estes Park in Rocky Mountain National Park. The terrain is mostly short boulder problems, with the bulk between VB and V4 and a few much harder ones, plus a few trad lines that range from easy 5.6 up to 5.11. Slabs, an arete and a wide crack decorate the southeast side. It is a handy stop for climbers with limited time: the walk is short compared with the big Lumpy Ridge formations, and the lower-angle features lend themselves to toproping. Scrambling is needed to reach the top anchors.

co_solaris.blurb: A granite crag on the south side of Boulder Canyon, just left of Avalon, made up of four buttresses divided by steep gullies and climbed on three levels: a lower tier, the main wall and a summit tower. Routes split evenly between bolted sport and trad, from an easy 5.5 up to 5.11, with most of the weight at 5.8 to 5.10. The main walls face west, so they are shady early and sunny later, which suits hot mornings or cool afternoons. A single 50 m rope and a rack of draws covers most lines. Expect a short creek crossing to get started.

co_sewemup_mesa.blurb: A remote sandstone cliff in the Unaweep country near Gateway, about an hour from Grand Junction. Almost everything here is trad, mainly moderate crack climbs with some roofs and a few multi-pitch lines, plus one bolted route and a single aid line. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.12, and more than half the routes sit at 5.10, so it rewards climbers comfortable on sustained cracks. Much of the wall is in shade, which makes it a good summer choice. The routes are grouped in clusters along the base, and the brushy walk between them is slow, so plan a quiet, self-reliant day.

co_south_canyon_point.blurb: A short conglomerate wall on the south rim of Castlewood Canyon State Park, south of Denver. Over half of the 22 routes are toprope lines, with five sport and five trad routes filling out the rest. Grades go from 5.6 to 5.11, with most between 5.8 and 5.10 and a handful of 5.11s. The rock is pebbly and sometimes crumbly, as is typical across the canyon, and the walls are short, so it works well for toprope days, newer leaders and climbers who want a quick session close to the city. Unlike many neighbouring rim walls, this one faces south and west.
